text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Former property magnate Juergen Schneider admits facts in charge sheet but does not admit guilt on the first day of his trial in Frankfurt
- Teachers want to go on strike in the German regional state of Hesse
- Wim Duisenberg is the new European Monetary Institute president. The Dutchman succeeds Alexandre Lamfalussy at a farewell celebration
- German President Roman Herzog praises entrepreneurial spirit in east Germany as 51 companies receive awards for their innovation
- German business believes in Hong Kong and expects expansion of its activities there and hardly any investors' flight from the territory
- Berlin building workers go on strike indefinitely
HANDELSBLATT
- Ex-property tycoon Juergen Schneider admits he gave false details to creditors when seeking loans
- Ifo economic institute says European economic and monetary union (EMU) will start with many participants
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl sticks to a strict deficit criterion for EMU entry
- Row between Deutsche Telekom and Otela escalates over a new fusing of networks
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- German President Roman Herzog honours enterpreneurs for their courage in eastern Germany
- Former real estate tycoon admits he falsified documents
- Health risks through new costs for medicines. Patients who are insured may not fetch necessary medicines because they are too expensive
- German business is confident of continuity in Hong Kong
DIE WELT

- The liberal Free Democrats, junior coalition partners in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition, and Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) criticise Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber over his euro-sceptical comments
- Ex-real estate businessman Juergen Schneider refuses to confess guilt in surprising opening of trial focused on the country's biggest property bankruptcy case ever
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) said it would move to Berlin by the year 2,000
- Berlin building workers go on strike
- There are more than 130,000 millionaires in Germany
- German President Roman Herzog says Germans can learn from the east German entrepreneurial experience --Bonn Newsroom +49 228 260 97160
